newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-OLAZABAL TWO SHOTS OFF LEAD IN TURESPANA MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-OLAZABAL TWO SHOTS OFF LEAD IN TURESPANA MASTERS.

text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal left himself with a golden opportunity of clinching his first title since returning to competition after shooting a five-under-par 68 in the Turespana Masters on Saturday.

The former U.S. Masters champion will start Sunday's final round in third place on 205, two strokes behind Argentine Jose Coceres and Briton Lee Westwood, who saw his overnight lead dwindle after a disastrous end to the day.
"The best thing is I'm not making mistakes ... two shots is not a lot," said Olazabal, although he admitted he was still not at his best with the driver.
The Spaniard, only recently returned to tournament play after lengthy foot problems, was able to close a six-shot gap on Westwood after the young Englishman's game fell apart in the last five holes.
Westwood had broken the course record with a 63 on Friday, and started the day in similar mood.
But he bogeyed at the 15th, and shot a double-bogey five on the next hole -- where a change in the wind seemed to affect him -- before missing birdie and eagle putts at the last two holes.
Westwood finished with a round of 68 while Coceres moved alongside him in the lead on 203 with the day's best round of 65.
Another Argentine, Eduardo Romero, was in fourth place, four shots off the lead, with Briton Paul Broadhurst and Paulo Quirici of Switzerland sharing fifth a further shot back.
